title: IVR Order Confirmation — SLO & health
description: W-0041 / P6-2. Every panel names a metric that a production call site actually records; UT-DASH-PII-04 walks the expressions back to those call sites and fails if a panel outruns the instrumentation. No panel carries a per-customer or per-order dimension: ivr.correlation_id is trace-only, and as a metric label it would turn every request into its own time series.

panels.title: Intake decisions by outcome
panels.description: Decision mix at the single intake exit. Rejections rising without a matching rise in volume points upstream at Sales payloads, not at IVR.

panels.title: Intake decision latency p95
panels.description: Wall time from task receipt to decision, measured at the same exit as the decision itself so the two cannot drift apart.

panels.title: Callback revalidate p95 by program (SLO: D-04, 5s)
panels.description: D-04 fixes the objective at 5s. This is the synchronous hop the customer-facing confirmation inherits.

panels.title: Callback delivery outcome
panels.description: Terminal delivery states from the outbox, including RETRY_EXHAUSTED which routes to admin review rather than to a pager.

panels.title: Callback transport vs semantic ACK, by contract
panels.description: HTTP status and semantic ACK are separate questions: a 200 carrying a rejection is a failed confirmation with a healthy transport. Split by contract so the current Golden Hour compat path is never averaged together with target v1.

panels.title: Fail-closed holds by reason (DO-06)
panels.description: Holding when a dependency cannot be proven healthy is designed behaviour. Read the proportion against intake volume, not the absolute count.

panels.title: Channel auto-disable, 10m window (DT-04)
panels.description: DT-04 auto-disables a channel at three failures in ten minutes. The window here matches the rule so the panel and the page agree.

panels.title: Business outcome rate (ARCH-06 §1)
panels.description: W-0041 declared these rates and could not draw them: ivr_call_results_total had no call site. It does now (ResultRepository, after commit). clamp_min keeps a division by an idle period from rendering as infinity, which reads like an incident rather than like silence. Runbook: docs/slo.md#business-outcome-rate

panels.title: Attempts dispatched vs results normalized
panels.description: The two counters bracket the call path. A persistent gap means attempts are leaving the scheduler and not coming back as results — dispatch succeeding while normalization stalls, which no single counter can show. Runbook: docs/slo.md#attempt-result-gap

panels.title: Confirmation windows that closed with no final result, by reason (ARCH-06 §1)
panels.description: A COUNT per hour, deliberately not a rate: the question is "how many orders", and a rate renders one lost order as 0.0003/s -- a number nobody reads as an order. One line per reason and programme, because the sweep closes a window under four reasons that mean different things, and only two of them open a ticket. NO_DISPATCH_BEFORE_DEADLINE is a job queued with no channel ever coming, or held by eligibility because none would; the capacity model (W-0054) says the shipped pool covers the modelled peak, so anything above zero on this line falsifies a model assumption, and IvrConfirmationDeadlineMissed opens a ticket to recalibrate it (runbook docs/slo.md#capacity-deadline-missed). ELIGIBILITY_NOT_EVALUATED_BEFORE_DEADLINE is an order eligibility never answered, so nobody decided it could be called: the eligibility loop is off, failing, or missing some orders, and anything above zero opens IvrConfirmationWindowsExpiringUnevaluated (runbook docs/slo.md#confirmation-windows-expiring-unevaluated). WINDOW_EXPIRED_BEFORE_FINAL_RESULT is a customer dialled and not reached in time, a dry run eligibility cleared, or an order held for review: routine, with no alert and no threshold -- each hold was counted as fail-closed when it was made, and IvrDownstreamFailClosedSpike pages on their proportion while the windows are still open. CALLING_HOURS_CLOSED_BEFORE_DISPATCH is the calling hours running out before a call could be placed: the calling day ending, not a fault. NO_DISPATCH_BEFORE_DEADLINE is the only line the capacity model speaks to; never recalibrate it, or add channels, over the other three.

panels.title: Orders the retired trusted-skip would have skipped (OD-18)
panels.description: A COUNT per hour, not a rate: the unit that matters is orders, and a rate renders one of them as a number nobody reads as an order. Every increment is an order Module 3 still marks with the old skip evidence and IVR now calls anyway -- the exact size of the behaviour change W-0123 could only infer, because no target database was reachable to count it. Zero confirms the inference. Non-zero is not an IVR fault and not an alert: it means M3 is still sending a producer-side signal it was asked to stop sending, and each one is a real extra call to a real customer. Runbook: docs/slo.md#legacy-skip-candidates

panels.title: Oldest dialable call still waiting (dispatch backlog)
panels.description: How long the oldest call attempt the dispatch claim would take right now has been waiting, sampled every 15s by each worker's scheduler loop from the claim's own conditions -- a revoked order, a paused queue or an attempt already ringing is not waiting. max across workers, never sum: they all read the same queue. Counted from the later of the due time and the calling window opening, so an attempt that fell due overnight starts from zero when dialling resumes, and the line is zero while the window is shut. A dialler that has stopped records no attempts, results or misses; this is the line that still moves. Pages above 60s held for ten minutes. Runbook: docs/slo.md#call-queue-backlog-aging

panels.title: Callback latency error-budget burn (D-04: 1% over 5s in 30 days)
panels.description: The share of callback deliveries slower than 5s, divided by the 1% the D-04 budget allows. 1 spends the 30-day budget in exactly 30 days; 14.4 spends it in about two. Three windows so a spike and a slow leak can be told apart: 1h reacts, 6h confirms, 3d shows the trend. Reads the le="5" bucket, which IvrTelemetry pins as a boundary so the objective never falls inside a bucket and gets interpolated across. Deliveries minus fast deliveries over a clamped total, so an idle period reads as zero burn rather than as an incident. No burn alert yet: multi-window thresholds need a production baseline (docs/slo.md section 10). Runbook: docs/slo.md#callback-revalidate-latency
